mainTopic: Whether the court gives food support from an absent husband's property to his wife, the reasons for שמואל's refusal, and how he answers the sources that seem to go against him.
overview: רב rules that the court gives food support (מזונות) from a husband's property to his wife when he has gone overseas. שמואל rules that it does not, though he says רב agrees for the first three months. Everyone agrees she gets support once the husband is known to be dead. The argument is only when there is no word of his death. רב זביד explains that שמואל worries the husband left her money, and רב פפא explains that he worries the husband told her to live on her earnings. The two reasons give different results for a grown woman whose earnings are not enough, and for a young wife whose earnings are enough. The גמרא then challenges שמואל from a משנה and from several ברייתות where the court gives support. Each time it answers that the husband had been reported dead. For the last ברייתא, רב ששת's answer about a third party is rejected. רב פפא instead explains it as a case of one witness, which is enough for the wife but not for the children's inheritance. Finally, רב חסדא and רב יוסף argue whether the 'something else' in that ברייתא means jewelry or charity, and the comparison of their views continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does the court give food support to a wife whose husband is away?
steps.stepSummary: רב says the court gives food support to a married woman from her absent husband's property. שמואל says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The court gives food support to a married woman. And שמואל said: the court does not give food support to a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about a woman whose husband went overseas without leaving her anything to live on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband owes his wife food support. The question is whether a בית דין may take money from his property for her while he is away. רב says yes and שמואל says no.

keyTerms.meaning: The court sets aside or apportions (money for support)
Food support, the husband's duty to feed his wife

phrases.english: The court apportions food support for a married woman.
phrases.notes: This is רב's opinion. His name comes just before these words, where the case of a husband who went overseas is introduced.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵין פּוֹסְקִין מְזוֹנוֹת לְאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ.
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: The court does not apportion food support for a married woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the מחלוקת for this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the court gives support from the absent husband's property. שמואל: it does not.

steps.title: שמואל says רב agrees for the first three months
steps.stepSummary: שמואל claims that רב agrees with him for the first three months, because a man does not leave his home empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: אבא (רב) agrees with me about the first three months, because a person does not leave his house empty.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל narrows the argument. For the first three months after the husband leaves, even רב agrees the court does not give support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We assume a man leaving on a trip provides for his home, at least in the short term. So in the first three months there is no need to touch his property. The מחלוקת applies only after that.

keyTerms.meaning: Abba, the personal name of רב

phrases.english: Shmuel said: Abba agrees with me
phrases.notes: אבא is רב's actual name, so שמואל is saying that רב agrees with him.

phrases.english: regarding the first three months,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אָדָם מַנִּיחַ בֵּיתוֹ רֵיקָן.
phrases.english: because a person does not leave his house empty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the מחלוקת from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the first three months, both agree the court gives no support, since we assume the husband left provisions.

steps.title: The argument is only when there is no news of the husband's death
steps.stepSummary: If the husband is known to have died, everyone agrees she gets support. They argue only when there is no word of his death. רב gives his reason: the husband's property is bound to her support.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they heard that he died, everyone agrees. They argue where they did not hear that he died. רב said: the court gives support, because his property is bound to her. And שמואל said: it does not give support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines exactly which case רב and שמואל are arguing about, and it gives רב's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the husband is known to be dead, she is supported from his estate, and nobody disagrees. While he may still be alive, רב says his property is already bound to her support. שמואל still says no, and his reason is explained next.

keyTerms.meaning: When they argue, the case they argue about
Bound or mortgaged as a legal obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think שמואל denies that the husband owes his wife support. He agrees she is owed support. He only holds that the court should not take money from the husband's property while he may be alive, for reasons the גמרא gives next.

phrases.english: Where they heard about him that he died,
everyone agrees.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי, בְּשֶׁלֹּא שָׁמְעוּ בּוֹ שֶׁמֵּת.
phrases.english: When they argue, it is where they did not hear about him that he died.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: פּוֹסְקִין, דְּהָא מְשׁוּעְבַּד לַהּ.
phrases.english: Rav said: The court apportions, since he is bound to her.
And Shmuel said: The court does not apportion.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ בּוֹ שֶׁמֵּת כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the מחלוקת further and adds רב's reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees there is support once his death is known. The מחלוקת is only when there is no news of his death. רב's reason is that the husband is bound to support her.

steps.title: What is שמואל's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל refuses to give support.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for שמואל's reasoning, since רב's reason was already given. This sets up the next two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's logic is clear: the husband is bound to support her. We still need to know why שמואל holds back, given that he agrees she is owed support.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: The question is about שמואל's view, since רב already gave his reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind שמואל's ruling in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why שמואל holds that the court does not give support from the absent husband's property.

steps.title: רב זביד: he may have left her a bundle of money
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד explains that the husband may have given his wife a bundle of money before he left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: Say that he handed her bundles of money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives the first explanation of שמואל: we suspect the husband already left her money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he may have left her money, taking more from his property could make him pay twice. So the court does not give support.

keyTerms.meaning: He gave her, put into her hands

phrases.aramaic: רַב זְבִיד אָמַר: אֵימָא צְרָרֵי אַתְפְּסַהּ.
phrases.english: Rav Zevid said: Say that he handed her bundles of money.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד אָמַר: אֵימָא צְרָרֵי אַתְפְּסַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל suspects the husband left her money, so the court does not take more from his property.

steps.title: רב פפא: he may have told her to keep her earnings instead
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the husband may have told her to live on her own earnings in place of support.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We are concerned that perhaps he said to her, "Take your earnings in place of your food support."
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different explanation of שמואל: the husband may have given up his right to her earnings and, in exchange, stopped owing her support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband may tell his wife to keep her earnings and support herself. If he did that, he owes her no support, so the court does not take from his property.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned, we take into account
Your earnings, the work of your hands

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא אָמַר לָהּ
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: We are concerned that perhaps he said to her:
"Take your earnings in place of your food support."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא אָמַר לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 4 that differs from רב זביד's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל suspects the husband traded her support for her earnings, so he owes no support.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a case where רב זביד's reason and רב פפא's reason lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two explanations of שמואל ever lead to a different ruling. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons lead to "no support" in the usual case. The גמרא looks for a case where they split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the answers in steps 5 and 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where the reasons of רב זביד and רב פפא give different results.

steps.title: The difference: a grown woman whose earnings are not enough
steps.stepSummary: The two reasons differ for a grown woman whose earnings do not cover her needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them for a grown woman whose earnings are not enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the case where the two reasons split: an adult wife whose own earnings are not enough to live on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she is a grown woman, he may well have trusted her with money. So by רב זביד's reason we assume he left her some, and she gets no support. By רב פפא's reason, even if he traded her support for her earnings, those earnings do not cover her needs, so the court gives her the rest from his property.

keyTerms.meaning: It is enough, it provides for her

steps.whatToRemember: רב gives support because the husband is bound to her. שמואל holds back, either because he may have left her money (רב זביד) or because he may have told her to live on her earnings (רב פפא). For a grown woman whose earnings are not enough, רב זביד's reason means no support, while רב פפא's reason means the court gives her what she is missing.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them for a grown woman, and it is not enough.
phrases.notes: "It is not enough" means her own earnings do not cover what she needs to live on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For a grown woman whose earnings are not enough: by רב זביד's reason the court gives no support, since he likely left her money. By רב פפא's reason the court makes up the shortfall.

steps.title: A second difference: a young wife whose earnings are enough
steps.stepSummary: Another case where רב זביד's reason and רב פפא's reason give different results: a קטנה whose earnings cover her needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else, they differ about a young wife whose earnings are enough to support her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question from step 7: here is another case where the two reasons lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband would not leave a bundle of money with a young girl, so רב זביד's reason does not apply and she would get support. But since her earnings are enough, he may well have told her to live on them, so by רב פפא's reason she gets no support. This is the reverse of the case in step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl who is not yet an adult (here, a young wife)
It is enough for her (her earnings cover her needs)

steps.whatToRemember: Two cases separate the reasons: a grown woman whose earnings are NOT enough (step 8), and a young wife whose earnings ARE enough. In each case, one reason applies and the other does not.

phrases.english: Alternatively,
a minor wife, and her earnings are enough for her.
phrases.notes: No one leaves a bundle of money with a young girl, so only רב פפא's reason can stop her from getting support here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, opposite case answering the same question from step 7, alongside the case given in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where רב זביד's and רב פפא's reasons lead to different results.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קטנה whose earnings suffice: רב זביד's worry about a bundle of money does not apply to her, but רב פפא's worry that he told her to live on her earnings does.

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל from the משנה of חנן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה shows חנן and בני כהנים גדולים arguing only about an oath, which implies everyone agrees she receives support, against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If a man went overseas and his wife asks for support, חנן says she swears at the end but not at the start. The sons of the High Priests disagreed and said she swears both at the start and at the end. They argue only about the oath, but everyone agrees we give her support!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to challenge שמואל, who said the court does not give support to a woman whose husband went overseas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the only argument is about when she must swear. That implies both sides agree she does get support from the court. This seems to go directly against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: The sons of High Priests (judges who disagree with חנן)
They only argue up to this point (on this one issue)

phrases.english: We learned: One who went overseas
and his wife is demanding support,
חנן says: She swears at the end,
phrases.notes: 'The end' means later, when she comes to collect her כתובה after he dies.

phrases.english: and she does not swear at the outset.
The sons of High Priests disagreed with him
and said: She swears at the outset and at the end.
They disagree only
regarding the oath,
but support, we give her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of רב זביד and רב פפא and attacks שמואל's basic ruling directly.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the court does not give support to a woman whose husband went overseas.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the משנה's only argument is about the oath, both sides must agree that she receives support, which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: שמואל: the משנה is about a husband reported dead
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains the משנה as talking about a case where they heard the husband died.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל explained it: the משנה is talking about a case where they heard that he died.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge by limiting the משנה to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband is reported dead, she is supported from his estate, so the משנה gives her support. שמואל's own ruling is about a husband who is simply away and alive. So the משנה does not go against him.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it (as being about a specific case)
When they heard that he died

phrases.english: שמואל interpreted it:
when they heard concerning him that he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about any husband who went overseas, so support is given even when he is alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only about a husband reported dead; when he is simply away, שמואל's ruling of no support stands.

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if the husband returns and claims he left her support, he is believed, which suggests the court gave her support while he was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If a man went overseas and his wife asks for support, the sons of the High Priests say she swears, and חנן says she does not swear. And if he came back and said, 'I set aside support for her,' he is believed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge שמואל again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that if the husband returns and claims he left her support, he is believed, so she must give back what the court gave her. That assumes the court gave her support from his property in the first place, while he was away. This seems to go against שמואל, who says the court gives no support.

keyTerms.meaning: I set aside money for her support

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁהָלַךְ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
phrases.english: Come and hear: One who went overseas
and his wife is demanding support,
the sons of High Priests say: She swears,
חנן says: She does not swear.
And if he came and said:
'I set aside support for her,' he is believed!
phrases.notes: Being believed means she has to pay back what the court gave her. So the court must have given her support while he was alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁהָלַךְ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to שמואל, this time from a ברייתא that assumes the court gave the wife support.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the court does not give support to a woman whose husband went overseas.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא assumes the court gave her support from the absent husband's property, and only discusses whether he is believed to reclaim it. That contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: Here too: they heard he died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer: the ברייתא is about a case where the husband was reported dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is talking about a case where they heard that he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses שמואל's answer from step 11 for the ברייתא as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The support was given only because of a report that he had died. So the ברייתא does not prove that a living husband who is away must support his wife.

phrases.english: Here too
it is when they heard concerning him that he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer of step 11 to the ברייתא of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about a husband known to be alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a husband reported dead, so support was given from his estate.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says he came back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the ברייתא says 'if he came and said,' so he is clearly not dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it says, 'If he came and said'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband died, how could he come back and speak? The wording of the ברייתא seems to show that this was never a case of a dead husband.

keyTerms.meaning: But it says (the wording shows otherwise)

phrases.english: But it says: 'If he came and said'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 13 from the wording of the ברייתא itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about a husband who died.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dead man cannot come back and speak, so the wording 'if he came' shows he was alive.

steps.title: He came back after a false report
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he came back after a rumor of his death turned out to be false.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: if he came back after the report of his death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection and closes the defense of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was a rumor that he died, so the court gave her support. Then he showed up alive, so the rumor was false. Support was given only because of the rumor, so שמואל's ruling for a husband known to be alive still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: After a report (a rumor of his death)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל defends his ruling by explaining both sources as cases where the husband was reported dead. In the ברייתא, he later returned and the report proved false.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא shows a husband who is simply away. The court gave support only because of the death report, which later turned out to be wrong.

phrases.english: If he came after the report.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem raised in step 14, saving the answer of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the wording to fit the limited case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'If he came' means he was alive and known to be alive the whole time.
steps.terutzMaskana: He came back after a false report of his death; the support was given because of that report.

steps.title: Another ברייתא where the court gave support
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if the court set support for the wife of a man overseas, what they set stays set, even if the husband returns and says she should have lived off her earnings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A man went overseas and his wife asks for support. If he comes back and says, 'Let your earnings cover your support,' he is allowed. If the court already set support for her, what they set stays set.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא to challenge שמואל. This ברייתא seems to show that a court does give support to a woman whose husband is away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes the court set support for her while the husband was overseas. That fits poorly with שמואל, who says the court should not give support because the husband may have arranged things differently. The ברייתא even says the court's ruling stands, so she does not pay it back.

keyTerms.meaning: "Let your earnings cover your support." The husband keeps no claim on her earnings and does not feed her.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who went overseas
and his wife is demanding support,
and if he came and said
"Let your earnings cover your support"
phrases.notes: He's claiming this was the deal he made with her before he left.

phrases.english: he is permitted.
If the court went ahead and set support,
what they set stays set.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁהָלַךְ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the previous ברייתא was settled, the גמרא brings a new ברייתא against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that the court does not give support to the wife of a man who went overseas.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא describes a court setting support during the husband's absence and keeps that ruling in force.

steps.title: Here too, they heard he died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא is also about a case where a report came that the husband died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is talking about a case where they heard that he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer it gave before. The court only set support because it was reported that the husband was dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband was believed dead, the court was not feeding a living man's wife against שמואל's rule. It was supporting her from his estate. When he later shows up alive, the report turns out to have been false, but what the court set stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, the same answer applies

phrases.english: Here too,
it is where they heard that he died.
phrases.notes: This is the same answer from steps 11–15: a rumor that he died, which later turned out false.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 with the answer already used in steps 13–15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ברייתא is about a husband who was reported dead.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The court gave support to the wife of a husband known to be alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court acted on a report of his death, so שמואל's rule was not broken.

steps.title: A ברייתא that says the court feeds the wife
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states outright that the court goes down to the absent husband's property to feed and support his wife, but not his children and not anything else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A man went overseas and his wife asks for support. The court goes down to his property and feeds and supports his wife, but not his sons and daughters, and not anything else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger ברייתא against שמואל. This one says plainly that the court takes from the husband's property to feed his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the court's support is the main ruling of the ברייתא, not a side detail. That clashes head-on with שמואל. The ברייתא also limits the support: the wife gets it, but the children do not, and nothing extra is given. This limit becomes important in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: They go down to his property, taking from his assets
They feed and provide for her

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who went overseas
and his wife is demanding support:
the court goes down to his property
and feeds and supports his wife,
but not his sons and daughters,
and not anything else!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁהָלַךְ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם וְאִשְׁתּוֹ תּוֹבַעַת מְזוֹנוֹת — בֵּית דִּין יוֹרְדִים לִנְכָסָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new and more direct ברייתא against שמואל, after step 17 settled the previous one.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the court does not give support to the wife of an absent husband.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא openly rules that the court takes from the absent husband's property to feed his wife.

steps.title: רב ששת: he already fed her through a third party
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the ברייתא is about a husband who arranged to support his wife through a third party.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It is talking about a man who supports his wife through a third party.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת defends שמואל by limiting the ברייתא to a special case. The husband had already set up a third party to support his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's worry is that maybe the husband made other arrangements for her, such as letting her live off her earnings. When we know he set up a שליש to feed her, there is no such worry. The court is simply carrying out his own arrangement.

keyTerms.meaning: A third party, someone appointed to handle the money

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It is about one who supports his wife
through a third party.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: בְּמַשְׁרֶה אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ עַל יְדֵי שָׁלִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the husband had set up support through a שליש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The court feeds the wife of any absent husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court only continues support the husband himself arranged, so this is no problem for שמואל.

steps.title: Then the children should get support too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת: if he arranged support through a third party, why shouldn't his sons and daughters be fed too?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, his sons and daughters should also be fed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת's answer. A husband who sets up support usually covers his children as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the children are not fed. If the court is just carrying out the husband's arrangement through a שליש, the children would normally be included. So the limit in the ברייתא does not seem to fit רב ששת's case.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is the case

phrases.english: If so,
his sons and daughters too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the case involves support through a שליש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Support arranged through a שליש should cover the children too, yet the ברייתא leaves them out.

steps.title: He arranged it only for the wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the husband set up support through a third party only for his wife, not for his children.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where he arranged it for this one, his wife, but not for that one, his children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת by narrowing the case even more. The husband only made the arrangement for his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the arrangement covered only the wife, then the court carries out exactly that. Nothing he set up includes the children. This explains why the ברייתא feeds the wife but not the children.

phrases.english: When he arranged it for this one,
and did not arrange it for this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the children in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case further: the arrangement was for the wife only.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any arrangement through a שליש would cover the whole family.
steps.terutzMaskana: Here the husband arranged support only for his wife, so only she receives it.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא state it without any condition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the ברייתא speaks in general terms and hints at no special arrangement like this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is it stated without any condition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב ששת's whole approach. The ברייתא states a plain rule and never mentions a third-party arrangement for the wife alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule stated in general terms should apply in general, not only in a narrow special setup. רב ששת's reading needs a very particular case that the ברייתא never mentions. Because of this, the גמרא drops his answer and looks for a new one.

keyTerms.meaning: Why is it stated as a flat, general rule?

phrases.english: Why is it stated without any condition?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the narrowed answer in step 21, and with it רב ששת's approach.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's reading, now narrowed to an arrangement for the wife only.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא states a general rule with no hint of such a narrow, special case.

steps.title: רב פפא: one witness said he died
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the ברייתא is about a case where a single witness reported the husband's death. Since she may remarry on that testimony, she also receives support.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: It is where she heard through one witness that he died. Since she could remarry based on one witness if she wanted, we also give her support.
steps.whatsHappening: After רב ששת's answer fails, רב פפא gives a new answer for שמואל. The ברייתא is about a woman whose husband was reported dead by one witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman may remarry based on one witness who says her husband died. Since that testimony is enough to let her remarry, it is also enough for the court to give her support. This also explains the limit: the testimony helps her, not the children, which is why only the wife is fed. The ברייתא is therefore about a husband reported dead, not a living absent husband, so שמואל's rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל holds that the court does not support the wife of a living absent husband. Every ברייתא that seems to say otherwise is explained as a case where his death was reported. רב פפא adds that even one witness is enough for her support, because one witness is enough for her to remarry.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב פפא ties her right to support to her right to remarry. Testimony that is good enough for one is good enough for the other, and this also explains why the children are left out.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
It is where she heard that he died
through one witness.
She, since if she wanted
phrases.notes: "She" stresses the wife, unlike the children. The single witness helps her only.

phrases.english: to marry based on one witness
she would be able to marry,
we also give her support.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כְּשֶׁשָּׁמְעָה בּוֹ שֶׁמֵּת בְּעֵד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב ששת's rejected answer (steps 19–22) with a new answer to the ברייתא in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New way of reading the case: a report of his death from one witness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא has the court feeding the wife of a living absent husband, against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court feeds her because one witness reported his death. That testimony lets her remarry, so it also gives her support, but only her and not the children.

steps.title: Why the sons and daughters are not fed
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא finishes his answer. The children cannot take over the estate based on one witness, so they also get no food from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But his sons and daughters cannot go down to his property and inherit based on one witness. So we also do not give them food from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes רב פפא's answer from the previous step. It explains why the ברייתא feeds the wife but not the children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One witness is enough for the wife to remarry, so for her the husband counts as dead and she is fed from his property. For inheritance we need two witnesses. So for the children he is not yet treated as dead, and they cannot take food from his estate either.

keyTerms.meaning: To go down to his property, meaning to take possession of it

steps.whatToRemember: One witness counts for the wife, who may remarry and so is fed. It does not count for the children, who cannot inherit and so are not fed. This answers the question of why the ברייתא treats the wife and the children differently.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new answer. It is the second half of רב פפא's answer from step 23, which continues here.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one witness can be accepted for one purpose, remarriage, and not for another, inheritance.

phrases.english: His sons and daughters,
since if they wanted to go down to his property
phrases.notes: 'Go down to his property' means take it over as heirs.

phrases.english: based on one witness, they could not go down to it,
we also do not give them food.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּנָיו וּבְנוֹתָיו, דְּאִי בָּעוּ לְמֵיחַת לִנְכָסָיו בְּעֵד אֶחָד לָא מָצוּ נָחֲתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's answer from step 23 by explaining the children's side of it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case (one witness) so that the wife and the children get different results
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If he counts as dead enough to feed the wife, the children should be fed too.
steps.terutzMaskana: One witness is enough for remarriage but not for inheritance, so only the wife is fed.

steps.title: What does 'something else' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by 'something else' (דבר אחר).
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'something else' the ברייתא mentions?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a side question. It asks what the words 'something else' in the ברייתא refer to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the court feeds the wife from the absent husband's property, but not the children and not 'something else'. The term is unclear, so the גמרא asks what exactly is meant. This is a request for clarification, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: Something else, an unclear item in the ברייתא

phrases.english: What is 'something else'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the children's support and opens a side question about a phrase in the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What item the phrase 'something else' refers to

steps.title: Jewelry or charity
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says 'something else' means jewelry. רב יוסף says it means charity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said it means jewelry. רב יוסף said it means charity.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question. Each one explains 'something else' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חסדא, the item is the wife's jewelry, which she normally gets beyond her food. According to רב יוסף, it is charity money that the husband would normally give. Each is an item the court might not pay for while the husband is away.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: jewelry.
Rav Yosef said: charity.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: תַּכְשִׁיט. רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: צְדָקָה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two answers to the question in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חסדא: jewelry. רב יוסף: charity.

steps.title: Comparing the two opinions begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins working out what each opinion implies. It starts with the view that 'something else' means jewelry.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says it means jewelry, all the more so...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts to work out what each opinion means for the other item, and the sentence continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All the more so' (כל שכן) signals a logical step from a stronger case to a weaker one. If the court does not pay even for the wife's jewelry, which is for her own benefit, it surely will not pay for something less personal. The rest of the comparison comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says, meaning according to this opinion

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is unfinished here. Do not try to complete the reasoning until the next lines.

phrases.english: The one who says jewelry, all the more so
phrases.notes: He means: according to רב חסדא, who says the court doesn't pay for jewelry. The sentence continues in the next lines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts drawing conclusions from the two opinions given in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens a כל שכן reasoning based on רב חסדא's view; the conclusion follows next.
